newsitem.title: USA: German, U.S. officials discuss Kohl-Yeltsin talks.
newsitem.headline: German, U.S. officials discuss Kohl-Yeltsin talks.

text.p: German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe conferred with U.S. officials Friday on the eve of talks between Germany and Russian leaders to ensure that the allies speak with one voice on NATO's plan to admit former Soviet bloc countries.
"We have to speak with one language in order to ensure the best results," Ruehe told reporters.

He said he was referring not only to Chancellor Helmut Kohl's scheduled meeting on Saturday with Russian President Boris Yeltsin but plans of other allied leaders, include President Bill Clinton, to meet with Yeltsin before NATO invites the first former Russian allies to become members.
Ruehe met with U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbott and two U.S. senators and then had a private lunch with Defence Secretary William Perry.

Sen. Richard Lugar, a senior Republican on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, said the senators and Ruehe went through a checklist to be sure the allies' positions on dealing with Russia was the same "and we found that it was."

NATO foreign ministers agreed last month to issue invitations in July for the first former Soviet bloc countries to join the alliance, and at the same time establish relations giving Russia a role in shaping Europe's defence arrangements.
Asked if allies had already worked out details of the new NATO relationship with Russia, Ruehe said: "All the details will be worked out. I think we can agree on that."
Lugar said the allies agreed that Russia must have a say in Europe's security arrangements but the hard part for both Russia and NATO would be to work out exactly how to do it.
